nativeAppearance.palette: Active QPalette supplied by the desktop

runtime.busyRefresh: Skip while an operation is running
runtime.delivery: Queued Qt signals on the GUI thread
runtime.draftPreservation: Keep focused editors and invalid text during refresh

review.scope: Native runtime review captures; no hardware write or game compatibility claim

extensions.previewPolicy: Native widget descriptions only. No HTML/CSS previews or fixed theme color tokens.

components.name: Section navigation
components.description: Six persistent sections, native selection and Alt+1 through Alt+6 shortcuts.

components.name: Tabbed settings
components.description: Scrollable schema groups for wheelbase, force feedback and peripheral settings.

components.name: Setting row
components.description: Typed draft editor, separate confirmed readback and persistent inline validation.

components.name: Draft actions
components.description: Explicit connect, read, disconnect, discard and apply actions with busy and conflict gating.

components.name: Input bench
components.description: Palette-aware QPainter steering with measured pedal values and unavailable states.

components.name: Profiles
components.description: Saved setup selection, editable metadata and a read-only value preview.

components.name: Game relay
components.description: Explicit start and stop actions; mode selection alone does not start the relay.

components.name: Compatibility and diagnostics
components.description: Observed statuses, selectable launch commands, relay output and diagnostic export.

narrative.overview: Mozaproxy is a native Linux desktop utility for observing wheel input, preparing settings and controlling the game relay. Qt 6 through PySide6 supplies the system palette, fonts, controls, focus treatment and dialogs. The interface follows the desktop theme.
keyCharacteristics: Six persistent sections with native list navigation and tabbed settings.
Confirmed device readings stay separate from editable drafts.
A palette-aware steering drawing and native pedal progress bars show measured input.
dos: Do use the active Qt palette, application font and native widget style.
Do show confirmed readings, saved profile values and drafts separately.
Do preserve invalid edits and display a repair message.
Do keep Apply, settings connection and relay start as explicit actions.
Do keep launch commands selectable and copyable.
Do report missing readings and ownership conflicts in text.
donts: Don't hardcode a web palette, bundle a UI font or style native controls with web CSS.
Don't invent telemetry or mark a write confirmed before verified readback.
Don't connect settings, write hardware or start the relay when a page or profile is selected.
Don't replace native controls with HTML previews or decorative dashboard cards.
